subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology (Acme Inc.)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@acme.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro + Discovery - follow-up and technical recap

Hi Alice / Tom,

Really great to meet earlier - thanks for the time. As promised, quick recap of the technical points we covered and the next steps so your engineering team can digest and confirm. Please let me know if I missed anything.

High-level goals you shared:
- Low-latency real-time responses for customer chat (p95 target <= 120ms token latency for single-turn prompts)
- High throughput for batch reranking jobs (target 10k requests/hour during peak)
- Strict data isolation; must run in customer VPC for PII-sensitive workflows

Pain points:
- Current endpoint is inconsistent: p95 latency spikes to ~600ms under load
- Cost per 1k requests is higher than budgeted due to inefficient batching and lack of KV caching
- Need an SLA for latency and reliability for upcoming product launch in June

Technical constraints and requirements we noted:
- Model family: preference for Llama/opt-compatible 13B/33B variants; you also mentioned interest in exploring quantized 8-bit variants if accuracy holds
- Typical request size: 50-150 tokens, median 80 tokens; rotor/chat history usually pinned at 3 messages
- Throughput shape: steady daytime traffic with two 2-hour peaks; burst capacity needed up to ~20k reqs/hr for Black Friday-like scenarios
- Networking: must be deployed in AWS us-west-2 VPC; customer-managed subnets and security groups

Suggested deployment topology (initial recommendation):
1) Dedicated Private cluster in your VPC (Redwood Private): 2x GPU worker pools
   - Latency pool (capped batching, KV cache warmers) for conversational endpoints
   - Throughput pool (large batch windows) for batch reranking jobs
2) Autoscaling policy with cold-warm nodes and burst capacity to handle peaks
3) Canary routing + fallback to a lower-cost quantized model when latency SLOs are at risk

SLOs discussed (for confirmation):
- Latency: p50 <= 40ms token latency, p95 <= 120ms token latency for conversational endpoints (single-turn + cached KV)
- Throughput: sustain 10k reqs/hr steady; handling bursts to 20k reqs/hr with degraded p95 target 250ms
- Availability: 99.9% for production routes

Attachments: I attached a short technical recap + sample latency CSV we generated from a similar workload.

Next steps (proposed):
- Aditya / Redwood infra team to draft a reference topology + cost/throughput estimate by Wed 3/30
- Acme to share anonymized sample traffic profile (token distributions & peak times) by Fri 4/1
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra/edge team - propose Tue 4/5 11:00am PT (please confirm)

Thanks again - looped in Aditya for the topology and detailed SLO planning.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-tdr-acme.pdf (summary)
Attachment: slo-latency-sample.csv (sample metrics)

From: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@acme.com>

Date: 2027-03-28T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro + Discovery - follow-up and technical recap

Thanks Marissa - this is excellent and aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) The 120ms p95 target is for end-to-end user-facing latency (includes our app serialization). What you note as token latency - please call out expected added application overhead (we estimate ~25-40ms) so we can map to our 120ms ceiling.
2) For models: our preference is to start with a 13B variant and evaluate accuracy/latency trade-offs before moving to 33B or quantized variants.
3) We'll share the anonymized traffic sample by Friday; Tom will pull logs and scrub PII.

Confirming the proposed Tue 4/5 11:00am PT for the deep-dive.

Best,
Alice
Director of Engineering, Acme Inc.
alice.bryant@acme.com

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive prep - initial topology + notes

Hi Alice / Tom - following up with an initial technical note ahead of Tue's deep-dive. This is a short primer to help your infra team prepare.

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Median request size: 80 tokens, max 400 tokens in rare long-form cases
- Target conversational p95 token latency budget: 120ms minus app overhead (~40ms) => backend p95 budget 80ms
- Using a 13B model family to start, evaluating 8-bit quantization for throughput pool

Preliminary topology recommendation:
- VPC Private Control Plane (managed by Redwood) communicating with worker pools over customer peered subnets
- Latency pool: 4x A10G-style-ish GPUs (or equivalent NVL/Tesla), concurrency tuned for low queueing (batch size 1-4, async kernel selection)
- Throughput pool: 8x A40-style-ish GPUs with aggressive batching (batch sizes 32-128 depending on request mix)
- Redis-backed KV cache for frequently seen prefixes; warmers to pre-populate during peak windows

Performance considerations and tests we suggest during the deep-dive:
- Synthetic replay of your anonymized traffic at production scale (10k -> 20k req/hr) to measure queuing effects
- Token-level latencies captured at the inference layer to separate model compute from networking/app overhead
- Quantization A/B tests to measure accuracy delta between FP16 and 8-bit quantized 13B

Cost/ops note:
- We'll provide a preliminary cost estimate in the follow-up doc - two pools as described typically run into an estimated monthly spend range (we'll detail GPU types and utilization assumptions)

I'll bring a short test plan and benchmark scripts to the deep-dive. Marissa - if you want, I can share a draft topology diagram to the Drive link.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
